extracted.intended_audience: NHMRC Investigator Grant applicants and peer reviewers (Australia; biomedical/health researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer review of NHMRC Investigator Grant applications, assessing proposed research (Knowledge Gain), applicant track record (relative to opportunity), and Research Impact using explicit weights and a 7‑point score scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge Gain (30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of proposed research and significance of knowledge to be gained. Assigned a 30% weight in overall assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated via sub-components: theoretical concepts and hypotheses (clarity, novelty, soundness); research design (appropriateness, rigor); robustness of methodology; contribution to the research area and health outcomes; and innovation in approach. Score descriptors (1–7) are defined for this element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical concepts and hypotheses (Knowledge Gain sub-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, novelty and soundness of the theoretical concepts and hypotheses underpinning the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether hypotheses are clearly stated, conceptually well‑founded, novel within the field, and logically connected to research aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design (Knowledge Gain sub-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness and rigor of the research design proposed to address the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the study design is fit for purpose, controls bias/ confounding appropriately, and aligns with the stated aims and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological robustness (Knowledge Gain sub-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness of the methodology proposed to produce reliable and valid results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methodological rigor, reproducibility, statistical/analytical plans, sample size/ power considerations, and risk mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to research area and health outcomes (Knowledge Gain sub-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the proposed work will advance the research field and contribute to health outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential significance, how findings would change understanding or practice, and plausible pathways to improved health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (Knowledge Gain sub-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of innovation in the proposed approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the approach applies new concepts, methodologies, technologies, or translates existing knowledge in novel ways that meaningfully advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track Record Relative to Opportunity (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's demonstrated capability and achievements, evaluated relative to the opportunities they have had. Assigned a 50% weight in overall assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must evaluate track record taking account of the applicant's career stage and available opportunities; track record is broken into sub-components (Publications 35%, Other Research Outputs 10%, Other Achievements 5%). The 'relative to opportunity' provision must be applied when interpreting outputs and achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications (35% of total)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality (not quantity) of selected publications and bibliometric indicators as evidence of research contribution; this sub-component contributes 35% of the total assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider quality over quantity, citations relative to field benchmarks, authorship position, and the applicant's self-identified five most significant publications which are evaluated in depth. Use field norms when interpreting citation metrics and authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Research Outputs (10% of total)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑publication research outputs such as patents, software, datasets, clinical guidelines, tools and resources. This sub-component contributes 10% of the total assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the significance, availability to the community (e.g., repositories, code/data sharing), utility, and contribution of these outputs to research translation or field advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Achievements (5% of total)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards, editorial/leadership roles, mentoring/training contributions, and translation activities. This sub-component contributes 5% of the total assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider leadership, service to the field, evidence of mentoring and training, and recognized contributions to translation of research into practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative to Opportunity provision (equity adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal adjustment in evaluating track record to account for differences in opportunities available to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must account for career interruptions (parental leave, caring duties, illness), career stage, geographic factors (working in lower-resource environments), discipline norms (e.g., clinical workload), and equity factors (including Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander identity). This provision modifies expectations about volume/tempo of outputs and achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Impact (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the potential and realized impact of the applicant's research; assigned a 20% weight in overall assessment and divided into two 10% sub-criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact is assessed across Reach and Significance (10%) and Applicant's Contribution to Impact (10%). Reviewers should use documented evidence to judge magnitude, pathways to impact, and attribution to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach and Significance (Research Impact sub-criterion, 10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic and sectoral reach, and magnitude of influence of the research. Contributes 10% of the total assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider geographic reach (local, national, international), sectoral reach (academia, policy, clinical, industry, community), and documented evidence of the magnitude of influence or uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Contribution to Impact (Research Impact sub-criterion, 10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which impact can be directly attributed to the applicant and their role in translation. Contributes 10% of the total assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess direct attribution of outcomes to the applicant's work, their role in the translation pathway, and documented evidence (e.g., citations in policy/guidelines, implementation records, stakeholder adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score descriptors (7-point scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scoring scale used across criteria: 7 (Outstanding, very rare), 6 (Excellent), 5 (Very good), 4 (Good), 3 (Adequate), 2 (Limited), 1 (Poor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each score descriptor is explicitly defined for each criterion; reviewers should apply the descriptor definitions when assigning scores to Knowledge Gain, Track Record elements, and Research Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators (Appendix B)
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑level performance indicators provided above the score descriptors for three broad elements: quality of the proposed research, potential for impact, and demonstrated capability of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indicators sit above individual criterion descriptors and are intended to guide interpretation of what constitutes higher vs lower performance across the three broad assessment elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit criterion weighting and sub-criterion weights (scheme design)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHMRC provides explicit numerical weights for top-level elements (Knowledge Gain 30%, Track Record 50%, Research Impact 20%) and sub-criterion weights (e.g., Publications 35% of total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guideline emphasizes transparent, numeric weighting and formal accommodation of 'relative to opportunity' adjustments; reviewers must apply these weights when combining scores into overall assessments. The design contrasts with more holistic approaches used by other funders.
